script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. SUBURBAN PARK - DAY

Children run and play on the jungle gym. Parents chatter on benches.

MRS. DAVIS (30s) enters, a look of exhaustion on her face. Her son, MIKE (10), clings to her hand.

MRS. DAVIS
(sighing)
Another day.

MIKE
Mom, come play with us!

MRS. DAVIS
(shaking her head)
Not today, buddy.

INT. DAVIS KITCHEN - NIGHT

Mrs. Davis cleans the dinner dishes while Mike plays a video game.

MIKE
Mom, can I invite Tim over for dinner tomorrow?

MRS. DAVIS
(sighing)
Sure, honey. But please, just keep it simple. I'm already overwhelmed.

MIKE
Okay.

Mrs. Davis stares out the window. Memories flood back.

EXT. DAVIS BACKYARD - MEMORY

Children play on a swingset. Mrs. Davis and a man, MR. JAMES (40s), sit on a blanket, laughing.

MR. JAMES
I wish we could do this every day.

MRS. DAVIS
(smiling)
Me too.

Suddenly, a car skids onto the grass. MR. JAMES stands up, shielding Mrs. Davis and Mike.

MR. JAMES
Stay back, Mike!

MRS. DAVIS
What's going on?

A man, MR. BROWN (30s), steps out of the car, holding a gun.

MR. BROWN
(screaming)
You stole my money!

Mr. James tries to reason with him, but Mr. Brown shoots him. Mrs. Davis screams and covers Mike's eyes.

EXT. DAVIS KITCHEN - PRESENT

Mrs. Davis snaps back to reality. She sets down the dish she's holding and wipes away a tear.

MRS. DAVIS
(whispering to herself)
I can't do this alone.

INT. MR. JAMES' HOUSE - DAY

Mrs. Davis knocks on Mr. James' door. He opens, surprised.

MR. JAMES
(happy)
Mrs. Davis! I wasn't expecting to see you.

MRS. DAVIS
(nervously)
I need your help. I can't keep living like this. I need a second chance.

MR. JAMES
(smiling)
You have it, Mrs. Davis. I'll be here for you.

EXT. SUBURBAN PARK - DAY

Mrs. Davis and Mr. James sit on a bench, watching their children play. Mike runs over and jumps into Mr. James' lap, laughing.

MRS. DAVIS
(smiling)
Thank you.

MR. JAMES
(smiling back)
For what?

MRS. DAVIS
For giving us a second chance.

FADE OUT.

THE END
